content: In chemistry, a formula unit refers to the empirical formula of an ionic or covalent network solid compound, which is used as an independent entity for stoichiometric calculations. It represents the simplest whole-number ratio of ions present in an ionic compound. For example, in ionic compounds like sodium chloride (NaCl) and potassium oxide (K₂O), the formula unit reflects the lowest ratio of their constituent ions. Similarly, in covalent network solids such as silicon dioxide (SiO₂) and carbon (in the forms of diamond or graphite), the formula unit describes the smallest representative structure. Ionic compounds do not exist as discrete molecules. Instead, they form extended lattice structures, and the formula unit represents the smallest reduced ratio of ions within the compound. This unit provides information about the types and numbers of atoms in the smallest representative portion of the substance.
